From the allusive (ishari) interpretation: ﴿Praise be to Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾ is an allusion to the bringing into existence of the two worlds, the world of subtlety (latafa) and the world of density (kathafa), and to the fact that the bringing into existence of the world of subtlety precedes the bringing into existence of the world of density. This is indicated by what is widely reported: Allah, Exalted is He, created the spirits four thousand years before the bodies.

﴿Who made the angels messengers﴾ in conveying His commands to whomever He wills of His servants, or as intermediaries through whom His will, glory be to Him, is executed in His creatures.

﴿Possessors of wings, two or three or four﴾ is an allusion to their differing in readiness (isti'dad).

﴿He increases in creation what He wills﴾ is general, encompassing dominion and other things. The increase has been interpreted as the bestowal of readiness to see Him, Mighty and Majestic is He, upon those who have done good, and more.

﴿Whatever mercy Allah opens to people﴾ is the increase alluded to and other things.

﴿None can withhold it, and whatever He withholds, none can release thereafter﴾. In this there is an allusion that His mercy, glory be to Him, has preceded His wrath, Mighty and Majestic is He.

﴿And if they deny you, then messengers before you were denied﴾ is a consolation for His beloved ﷺ and a guidance to his heirs to be patient with the harm their enemies inflict upon them, with their denial of them and their rejection of them.

﴿And it is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir clouds, and We drive them to a dead land and revive thereby the earth after its death﴾. His custom, exalted is He, in reviving the earth is in this manner. Likewise, when He, glory be to Him, wills to revive the land of the heart, He first sends the winds of will (irada), which stir the clouds of love (mahabba). Then comes the rain of generosity and solicitude (inaya), which causes to grow in the heart the fragrant herbs of the spirit, the flowers of expansion (bast), and the blossoms of lights, and life becomes good.

﴿Whoever desires honor—to Allah belongs all honor﴾ is an allusion that true honor is not attained without annihilation (fana'). Do not neglect the hadith: "My servant does not cease to draw near to Me through supererogatory acts..." etc.

﴿And Allah created you from dust﴾, which is the furthest of created things from the Presence (hadra) and the lowest and densest of them.

﴿Then from a sperm-drop﴾, in which there is some kind of subtlety, ﴿then He made you into pairs﴾. This is an allusion to the pairing that came about for them of the subtle, sublime spirit and the dense, lowly body, which is the starting point of readiness for standing before the worlds of the unseen and the witnessed.

﴿And the two seas are not alike﴾. It has been said that this means: the sea of divinely bestowed knowledge (al-'ilm al-wahbi) and the sea of acquired knowledge (al-'ilm al-kasbi). This one, that is, the sea of divinely bestowed knowledge, ﴿is sweet, palatable, pleasant to drink﴾, because it is free of the accidents of doubts and illusions. ﴿And this one﴾, that is, the sea of acquired knowledge, ﴿is salty and bitter﴾, because of the hardship of reflection, the bitterness of acquisition, and the arising of doubts, hesitation, and disturbance in it.

﴿And from both you eat tender flesh﴾: subtle allusions by which you are nourished and strengthened for works. ﴿And extract ornaments to wear﴾, which are the noble characteristics, beautiful manners, and praiseworthy states that bring their possessor adornment.

﴿And you see the ships﴾, the vessels of the Sharia and the Tariqa, ﴿plowing through it﴾, running.

﴿That you may seek of His bounty﴾ by arriving at His Presence, Mighty and Majestic is He, by doing that.

﴿O mankind, you are the poor toward Allah﴾ in all your affairs. The degrees of poverty vary, and whenever a person draws closer to Him, Mighty and Majestic is He, his poverty toward Him increases, because love increases then. Whenever passion increases, the lover's poverty toward the beloved increases, until he passes away.

﴿And Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy﴾. In this is whatever good tidings it contains.

﴿Only those fear Allah, from among His servants, who have knowledge﴾, that is, those who have knowledge of Him, exalted is He, and of His affairs. The more they increase in knowledge, the more they increase in fear, because His greatness, Mighty and Majestic is He, becomes manifest to them, and because in relation to Him, exalted is His station, they are nothing.

﴿Then We bequeathed the Book to those We chose of Our servants, and among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds by permission of Allah﴾. It has been said: the one who wrongs himself is the wayfarer (salik), the moderate one is the wayfarer who is also drawn (majdhub), and the foremost one is the drawn one who is also a wayfarer. The wayfarer is the one who seeks nearness, and the drawn one is the one who has been brought near. The drawn wayfarer is the one absorbed in the perfections of nearness, passed away from his own self and subsisting through his Lord, Mighty and Majestic is He.

﴿And they say: Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us the grief﴾, the grief of imagining separation. There is no grief greater for the lover than the grief of imagining that his beloved has forsaken him and turned away from him.

﴿Indeed our Lord is Forgiving, Appreciative﴾. So it is no wonder that He removes that from us and secures us from severance and estrangement.

﴿He who has settled us in the abode of permanence from His bounty; there touches us not therein fatigue, nor touches us therein weariness﴾. "Fatigue" is the weariness of the bodies and their toil through acts of obedience for drawing near to Him, glory be to Him. "Weariness" is the exhaustion and agitation of the hearts from imagining severance, rejection, and the abandonment of the Beloved. It has also been said: there touches us not therein the toil of striving to obtain whatever we desired, nor touches us therein the weariness of imagining the loss of whatever we have obtained.

They have indicated that all of this is from the bounty of Allah, Exalted is He, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is the Possessor of Great Bounty. This is it. We ask Allah, Exalted is He, from His sweet bounty, that which splits open the bitterness of the envious, that which shatters the heart of every enemy, and that which revives the heart of every loving, affectionate one.
